name: Marc Forsmark Nielsen
title: Product Engineer
subtitle: Frontend, UX and AI-powered products
statement: I build AI tools and data-heavy products that people in regulated work can understand and trust. I take features from the user problem through design to release.

roles.title: Lead Frontend Developer
points: Lead frontend development of a medical data visualization platform built with Lit and TypeScript.
Drive adoption of AI tooling in the engineering workflow.
Improve the team's delivery process: sprint planning, testing practice and documentation that supports compliant releases.
Work across teams on product reliability and regulatory requirements for medical software.

roles.title: Frontend Developer
points: Built SaaS web applications with React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
Rewrote the rendering logic for large, data-heavy forms, which made them substantially faster.
Designed data entry flows for high-volume input, with focus on speed and accuracy.
Implemented an accessible design system together with designers in Figma.

roles.title: Lead Frontend Developer
points: Led frontend development of the company's IoT data platform in React.
Reworked user flows and visual design across the product.
Mentored junior developers and promoted engineering best practices across the team.

roles.title: Software Developer
points: Full-stack development, and a React platform for data collection and visualization.
Rewrote the IoT node graph traversal from Python to Go, with better data structures and lower algorithmic complexity.
Developed Java plugins that connect Universal Robots arms to the platform.

education.institution: Zealand Academy of Technologies and Business

principles.title: People decide
principles.body: AI suggests, people stay in control. Every AI feature shows what it did and why, and a person can check it, change it or turn it off.

principles.title: Built to be checked
principles.body: In regulated work, tests, documentation and traceability are part of the product, not paperwork after it.

principles.title: Problem first
principles.body: Start with who uses it and in what situation. The stack comes after, and it stays boring where it can.
